newsitem.title: USA: Ford Q4 EPS estimate seen lowered - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Ford Q4 EPS estimate seen lowered - analyst.

text.p: Burnham Securities Inc analyst David Healy said he expects to drop his fourth quarter estimate for Ford Motor Co to $0.85 or $0.90 a share from $1.15 because of charges to cover early retirements and continuing losses in South America.

Ford Chief Financial Officer John Devine told analysts during a conference call Wednesday the fourth quarter consensus estimate of $1.15 is too high given expected further losses in South America and up to $400 million in charges for early retirement costs, Healy said.
"At this point, I can't quarrel with $0.85 or $0.90 cents for the quarter," Healy said.
Ford lost $226 million from South America in the third quarter, almost all of that from Brazil, where it has experienced higher than expected launch costs.
"Brazil is likely to be just as bad" in the fourth quarter, said Nicholas Lobacarro, an analyst at Bear Stearns.
Lobacarro said he has not changed his $1.15 estimate. But added, "Before, I would say there was an opportunity for upside. Now, I would say there are opportunities for downside."
Ford told reporters earlier Wednesday it expects to report fourth quarter earnings that are higher than the $660 million or $0.48 a fully diluted share for the 1995 period.
For the third quarter, Ford had earnings of $686 million or $0.56 a share. The numbers include net one-time gains of $37 million, and compare to $357 million or $0.27 a year ago.
